messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple container restarts detected on gpu-node-42 for model redwood-7b-prefetch. Recent pattern: OOM during prefetch of large context windows. Count=3 in 2m. Severity=P1. Paging #incidents #oncall
sara-oncall: taking pager. pulling k8s events + docker logs now. tagging @raj in case this needs infra-level action.
raj: looking. any correlated CUDA errors in dmesg? possible driver reset?
sara-oncall: yes, seeing repeated `CUDA_FATAL` + kernel log with context allocation failures. paste logs:```OOM when allocating tensor (size=10.5GB) at prefill step; container restarted with exit code 137```
mike: are these coming from a small set of customers or broad traffic?
ops-bot: telemetry snapshot: 12% of requests in last 3m had context_length > 65k tokens; error rate spiked from 0.2% -> 4.8%. Hot nodes: gpu-node-42,gpu-node-43.
sara-oncall: looks like a few large-context jobs (batching with very long prompts) overloaded the hotpool. immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch on hotpool for redwood-7b 2) apply streaming/trimming policy 3) scale hotpool replica +1 4) route new large-context requests to dedicated coldmodel if available. executing step 1 now.
raj: confirm kube patch to set PREFETCH=false on deployment redwood-7b-hotpool. also increasing eviction priority for requests > 50k tokens. applying.```kubectl patch deployment redwood-hotpool -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"prefetch":"false"}}}}}'```
sara-oncall: patch applied. rolling pods. starting a manual drain on gpu-node-42 to move existing pods off for safe restart (`kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets gpu-node-42 --delete-local-data`).
infra-lead: agree with drain. I'll queue a node reboot if kernel shows memory fragmentation. starting cordon + reboot if restarts continue.
paul-cs: any customer-facing impact? seeing alerts from one customer with high-latency errors on embeddings endpoints. need a short status blurb for support.
sara-oncall: customer-impact: intermittent failures for very long-context requests; ~0.5% of total requests during the spike, higher for that customer. no data exfiltration; retries would succeed once routed to fallback. suggested blurb: "We're mitigating an infrastructure issue causing failures for very long requests. We're routing affected requests to a fallback path; most traffic restored. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause." approve?
paul-cs: good, posting now to affected support tickets and customers.
raj: metrics look better after prefetch disable + extra replica. OOMs stopped on gpu-node-42 after pods recreated. GPU free memory returned to expected baseline.
mike: any longer-term fixes?
sara-oncall: follow-ups: (a) implement request-size circuit breaker in gateway to reject >64k tokens or return structured guidance to split, (b) prefer streaming prefill with KV trimming for long contexts, (c) add kernel-level OOM analyzer to correlate allocations to request ids, (d) add per-tenant large-context rate limits on hotpool.
infra-lead: I'll take (c) and (d). raj take (a) with gateway team. sara, can you own rollout of streaming prefill policy?
sara-oncall: yes. will create RFC + rollout plan. scheduling canary tomorrow.
ops-bot: Incident summary (automated): root cause likely large-context prefetch allocation spike causing GPU memory exhaustion on hotpool nodes. Mitigations performed: disabled prefetch on hotpool, scaled +1 replica, drained affected node, routed large-context to fallback. Customer impact: limited, targeted to large requests; support notified. Next steps assigned.
raj: handing off monitoring + follow-up to on-call rotation starting 1765510200. I'll be offline in 30m.
sara-oncall: handing off to @raj for next rotation. leaving notes in pager duty and incident doc. :white_check_mark:
paul-cs: thx team. will update customers after we collect RC details.
